description: Risk-oriented behavioral scenarios and human-review rubrics; not agent-execution results

cases.scenario: Solution-first request with unsupported implementation choice
cases.input: Stakeholder: Build a new dashboard immediately. The underlying problem and success criteria were not supplied.

checks.criterion: Elicitor investigates the underlying need and success signal before accepting the dashboard as a requirement.
Does not convert the requested dashboard into an approved requirement or architecture without evidence.

cases.scenario: Dependent decisions about the end of a billing retry window
cases.input: Define a retry policy for a subscription. The grace-window origin is undecided; the last allowed instant and time zone depend on that choice. No owner has approved any of these decisions.

checks.criterion: Identifies the unresolved start of the window as a prerequisite to precise retry timing.
Does not silently decide the deadline, time zone, or late-arriving charge outcome.
Requests the next material decision rather than an unrelated exhaustive questionnaire.

cases.scenario: Known evidence should not be requested again
cases.input: Source S1 (authorized product policy): refund limit is 2 per user per rolling 365 days. The only unknown is whether pending refunds count toward the limit.

checks.criterion: Identifies the pending-refund treatment as unresolved and relevant to the rule.
Does not ask the user to restate the limit or time window already established by S1.

cases.scenario: Adjacent discovery must not silently expand the Change Boundary
cases.input: Approved change: expose a read-only refund count. During discovery a stakeholder suggests redesigning all refund processing; no scope authority approved the expansion.

checks.criterion: Preserves the approved read-only boundary and identifies the redesign as a separate proposal requiring authorization.
Does not include refund-process redesign in the current approved change or work items.

cases.scenario: Non-functional requirement lacks measurable fit criterion
cases.input: System shall be fast under load. No workload, performance metric, acceptable limit or verification environment has been authorized.

checks.criterion: Identifies missing workload/context, measure, justified threshold, and verification method for objective acceptance.
Does not fabricate a latency number, percentile, or workload to make the requirement appear testable.

cases.input: A renewal attempt is permitted during grace period; the business did not define whether an attempt exactly at the grace-end timestamp is permitted or how in-flight attempts behave.

checks.criterion: Makes temporal trigger, inclusive/exclusive boundary, and in-flight behavior explicit as unresolved semantic concerns.
Does not claim the temporal property is formally verified or realized by an unspecified implementation.

cases.scenario: Scenario set needs counterexamples and identity preservation
cases.input: Requirement R1: only the owner can change an address. Existing scenario SC-7 covers an owner update. Need to evaluate a non-owner request and a concurrent owner update. No test framework specified.

checks.criterion: Preserves SC-7 identity while exploring relevant authorization counterexample and concurrency conditions.
Does not turn scenario identity into test filenames or generate executable tests without authorization.

cases.input: Policy P1 says refunds are permitted within 7 days. Policy P2, from a different authority, says 14 days. There is no supersession decision. Spec R1 says 7 days.

checks.criterion: Reports a material conflict with source references and the missing authority decision.
Does not silently choose the newest or preferred policy and label the specification sufficient.
Does not edit the requirement during read-only validation.

cases.scenario: Safe vertical slicing of payment changes
cases.input: Authorized change: retry failed card charges with deduplication guarantee. Proposed slice A activates retries but postpones idempotency until slice B. Finance impact is material.

checks.criterion: Flags the initial slice as unsafe because it omits a required deduplication guarantee.
Does not split a critical guarantee across an unsafe intermediate release or invent design choices.

cases.scenario: End-to-end Requirements handoff stops at authorized planning level
cases.input: Stakeholder needs a refund-count endpoint and provides user, time-window and status semantics but no database design. Ask for requirements, validated scenarios and a granular implementation-ready backlog where supported.

checks.criterion: Routes through the necessary Requirements capabilities and reports validation readiness for the next step.
Produces coherent work items linked to approved requirements and applicable scenarios, at the granularity justified by current evidence.
Does not invent database schema, internal code tasks, commit, automated tests, or claim implementation completed.
